Candidate competition is a plausible objective change, but harder negatives do not guarantee better ranking. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study comparing random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive samplers found dataset-dependent tradeoffs: random sampling favored head items; popularity-based sampling balanced popularity bands while sometimes reducing overall accuracy. These results support controlled sampler ablations, not a universal hard-negative recipe. [Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276). NeurIPS 2024’s Pairwise Softmax Loss (PSL) identifies softmax’s sensitivity to false negatives and proposes alternative pairwise activation functions to improve robustness and ranking alignment. This is relevant evidence for changing the loss while retaining BERT4Rec, although it does not establish gains on the specified Amazon task. [PSL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163).

Practical hypothesis: retain masked-target BERT4Rec and appended-mask inference; compare multi-negative sampled cross-entropy against a PSL-style objective. Draw a uniform candidate pool, optionally introduce a small fraction of moderately hard negatives scored by the same network, and exclude target IDs, reserved tokens and known training positives. Deduplicate candidates; warm up before hard mining and sweep hardness/temperature conservatively. These safeguards are proposed experiments, not demonstrated improvements; unobserved items can still be false negatives. Avoid describing sampling-probability correction as making finite sampled softmax unbiased: NeurIPS 2025 establishes a general bias limitation for subset-only softmax estimators. [Theory](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/42b7c2f6d320d1fe1afa899a6319d6d7-Abstract-Conference.html). Use one jointly trained network/checkpoint per category, preserve the fixed training limits, and select solely by four-category macro validation HR@10; inspect Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics margin tails as secondary diagnostics.
